original_question: Find the asymptotic value of L(m,n), the minimum number of distinct point-to-line distances determined by a set of m points and a set of n lines in the plane.
target_in_paper: Section 9, Problem 38 in the latest arXiv version of arXiv:1406.1949 (the same problem appears as Section 7, Problem 34 in the June 7, 2014 draft PDF): determine the asymptotic value of L(m,n), after defining L(m,n) to be the minimum number of distinct distances between a set of m points and a set of n lines in ℝ^2.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct target almost exactly: it uses the paper’s notation L(m,n), it asks for the asymptotic value, and it correctly identifies the objects involved as a set of m points and a set of n lines in the plane, counting distinct point-to-line distances.
missing_details: The ambient space should be stated explicitly as the Euclidean plane ℝ^2.
L(m,n) should be defined explicitly as a minimum over all finite sets P of m distinct points and all finite sets ℒ of n distinct lines in ℝ^2.
The distance must be specified as the usual Euclidean distance from a point to a line.
It should be made explicit that the quantity being counted is |{dist(p,ℓ) : p ∈ P, ℓ ∈ ℒ}|, so only point-to-line distances are counted, not point-point or line-line distances.
The variables m and n should be identified as positive integers.

The asymptotic question is bivariate: the problem asks for the order of growth of L(m,n) as a function of m and n, with no extra geometric assumptions or size relation between m and n built into the statement.
refined_question: Let L(m,n) be the minimum possible value of |{dist(p,ℓ) : p ∈ P, ℓ ∈ ℒ}|, where P ⊂ ℝ^2 is a set of m points, ℒ is a set of n lines in ℝ^2, and dist(p,ℓ) is the usual Euclidean distance from the point p to the line ℓ. Determine the asymptotic order of L(m,n) as a function of the positive integers m and n.
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation. The paper introduces L(m,n) precisely as the minimum number of distinct distances between m points and n lines in ℝ^2, with point-line distance taken in the usual sense, and then immediately poses the open problem of finding its asymptotic value. In the latest arXiv version this is numbered as Problem 38 in Section 9; in the earlier PDF draft available from the author’s site it is Problem 34 in Section 7, with the same mathematical content. I therefore kept the scope exactly at the point-line problem and only added the explicit minimization, the ambient space, the quantifiers, and the exact distance set so that the question is fully stand-alone and paper-faithful.
